elidable.contract: No observable side effects; result determined purely by arguments. The JIT relies on this to cache and reorder calls.
elidable.violation_signal: Assignment to self.*, module globals, or a call to anything not itself elidable/pure inside the decorated function.

elidable_promote.contract: Same as elidable, plus arguments are promoted (treated as JIT-time constants) before the call.

unroll_safe.contract: Loop bound must be provably JIT-compile-time-constant/small, or risks trace explosion.
unroll_safe.violation_signal: Loop bound derived from len() of something not promoted, or a runtime-read field.

dont_look_inside.contract: JIT should not trace into this function's body.
dont_look_inside.violation_signal: Placed on a function that's on an actual hot path (reachable from a JitDriver merge point) without a comment explaining why -- sometimes deliberate, always the author's call.

promote.contract: Argument is treated as a JIT-time constant at this call site.
promote.violation_signal: Promoting a value that genuinely varies at runtime causes trace explosion; promoting self on an object whose relevant fields aren't actually immutable is a correctness hazard -- see immutability-contract-mismatch-promoted.

loop_invariant.contract: Function's result is invariant across loop iterations for a given trace.

purefunction.contract: Legacy name/alias-adjacent to elidable in some PyPy versions -- verify against the actual checkout's jit.py before relying on this.

isvirtual.contract: Query whether the JIT currently represents an object as a virtual (not yet heap-allocated).
isvirtual.violation_signal: Not a correctness contract in the same sense as the others -- informational.

loop_unrolling_heuristic.contract: Heuristic controlling whether a loop gets unrolled.

_immutable_fields_.contract: Listed fields never change after construction. Trailing '?' (which can appear before a '[*]' list-marker suffix, e.g. 'closure?[*]') marks a field as quasi-immutable -- assigned at most once after construction, not truly const.
_immutable_fields_.violation_signal: A field listed WITHOUT the '?' marker that is reassigned in any method other than __init__. See scan_immutability_contracts.py.
_immutable_fields_.marker_ordering_gotcha: The '?' comes BEFORE '[*]' for list fields ('closure?[*]'), not after ('closure[*]?'). Getting this wrong produces false positives on already-correctly-marked fields -- see pypy_non_bugs.md.

_attrs_.contract: Declares the full set of attributes an RPython class instance may have -- a different mechanism than _immutable_fields_, also annotator-recognized.
_attrs_.violation_signal: Not currently checked by any v0.1 scanner.
